newsitem.title: SPAIN: Jail term for Spain's ex-Banesto chairman.
newsitem.headline: Jail term for Spain's ex-Banesto chairman.

text.p: Spain's High Court sentenced former Banesto Bank chairman Mario Conde to six years in prison for fraud on Thursday in the first verdict arising from the country's biggest financial scandal.

Conde was also ordered to pay more than $5.0 million in the first in a series of trials on charges that he and his closest associates committed massive fraud that led to the 1993 collapse of Banco Espanol de Credito-Banesto.
"We convict Mario Conde for the crime of misappropriation of funds and falsifying public documentation on penalty of six years in prison..." Magistrate Ventura Perez said.
Conde will be tried later this year on related charges that carry even stiffer jail sentences if he is convincted.

The case that was decided on Thursday centred on a $4.2 million payment made in 1990 by Banesto to Argentia Trust, a shadowy company based on the Lesser Antilles island of St. Vincent, a popular tax haven.
Conde was ordered to pay Banesto back the money and was also fined $70,000. When the sentence was handed down, Conde was free on bail.
